specification.title: A nested scope fails, and PostgreSQL rejects its ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Write the marker `outer`, and make sure the write was sent.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure the write was sent.
Checkpoint `inner-after-write`: report the backend PID. The runner sees the savepoint's subtransaction lock.
Arm the client-side fault (the next ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT is rewritten to name a savepoint that does not exist, so PostgreSQL rejects it), then raise an application error in the nested scope.
When the fault fires, before the framework sees its error, the adapter's driver layer reports checkpoint `after-fault` (the backend PID): the runner records the fault's effect on the server.
The outer scope catches the nested scope's error.
Checkpoint `after-outer`, after the outer transaction's API has returned: report the same backend PID. The runner records whether that session is still inside a transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If the API reports that the outer transaction committed, PostgreSQL committed it, with the outer scope's writes and none of the failed nested scope's writes.
When the outer transaction's API has returned, the connection that ran it is no longer inside a transaction.

execution.description: Positive control: reads the command tag of PostgreSQL's reply to COMMIT, reports a COMMIT error as a failure, and discards a connection whose ROLLBACK failed. It starts a transaction at the isolation level requested of it.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A client-side injection in the adapter's driver layer: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT is rewritten before it is sent, to name a savepoint that does not exist. PostgreSQL rejects it with 3B001, which aborts the current subtransaction (the savepoint's). The error is PostgreSQL's; the trigger is artificial.
fault.injection_point: The framework's rollback of the nested scope.
fault.preconditions: The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_server: The savepoint's subtransaction is aborted: the session is "idle in transaction (aborted)" while the top-level transaction stays in progress. A ROLLBACK TO the existing savepoint recovers it; a COMMIT without recovery is answered with ROLLBACK, and commits nothing.
fault.expected_client: A PostgreSQL error from the nested scope's rollback.

knowledge: The framework receives PostgreSQL's error (3B001) for the savepoint rollback. If it then sends COMMIT without recovering, it receives the command tag ROLLBACK.

api_outcome.basis: a savepoint rollback had failed, so the control ended the transaction with ROLLBACK instead of COMMIT
api_outcome.contract: The correct control reports committed only when PostgreSQL answers COMMIT with the command tag COMMIT, reports any other tag as a rollback, and reports a COMMIT that raised as a failure. After a failed savepoint rollback, it ends the transaction with ROLLBACK instead of COMMIT. It starts a transaction at the isolation level requested of it.

error.message: a savepoint rollback failed, so the transaction was rolled back
application error: the nested scope fails

preconditions.description: the write of marker "outer" had reached PostgreSQL at `outer-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "inner" had reached PostgreSQL at `inner-after-write` (a subtransaction lock, in pg_locks)
the client-side fault (rewrite) fired exactly once
the nested scope's error reached the outer scope, which handled it
the runner observed the transaction's session after the outer API returned
PostgreSQL rejected the rewritten ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT (3B001)
the rejection aborted only the subtransaction: the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)", and the top-level transaction was still in progress
preconditions.detail: at `after-fault`: session "idle in transaction (aborted)", backend_xid 37733; transactionid locks [37733]; top-level pg_xact_status: in progress
